candidates.title: Predicting Dimensional Errors in FDM Printing Using Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Dimensional accuracy in additive manufacturing represents a critical factor for the quality of functional parts. This work presents a predictive model based on artificial neural networks to estimate and reduce geometric deviations in polylactic acid parts processed by fused filament fabrication. Using a response surface experimental design, the influence of extruder temperature, bed temperature, printing speed, and layer height on the hole diameter relative to its computer-aided design was evaluated. The geometric discrepancy fed the training of the predictive model, which was subsequently coupled with a genetic algorithm to determine optimal manufacturing parameters. The optimized approach successfully reduced the predicted dimensional error to a minimum of 1.59%, demonstrating its applicability in automated calibration for additive processes.

candidates.title: A data-efficient PINN-Bayesian optimization framework for state variable active filter design
candidates.abstract: Designing an analog active filter is rarely a single-target exercise: cutoff frequency, quality factor, gain, power draw, total harmonic distortion (THD), and sensitivity to component spread all have to be pulled into line at once. In practice, this still means loop after loop of SPICE runs and manual tweaking, which eats up design time and computing budget alike. This paper instead builds a Bayesian Optimization loop around a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) surrogate to automate the synthesis of State Variable Filters (SVFs). Adaptive sampling of the design space, LTspice-based circuit simulation, PINN surrogate modeling, and Bayesian Optimization are brought together so that optimal component values can be located with far fewer costly simulation runs. By incorporating the governing circuit relationships, analytical transfer function, frequency–response characteristics, and stability constraints into PINN training, the proposed surrogate captures the nonlinear relationship between component values and filter performance while maintaining physical consistency. That trained surrogate then drives the Bayesian search, quickly narrowing in on Pareto-optimal filter configurations across cutoff frequency accuracy, passband gain, quality factor, power consumption, THD, and sensitivity. The resulting design reached a cutoff frequency of 10.01 kHz, a gain of 0.998, a quality factor of 0.709, an estimated active-filter power of 12.4 mW, THD of 0.32%, and a sensitivity index of 0.048, with Bayesian Optimization converging in 37 iterations and an average run time of 42.8 s. Benchmarked against Random Search, Particle Swarm Optimization, Genetic Algorithm, and Differential Evolution, the proposed framework consistently reached lower objective values than any of them. A TL084-based hardware prototype backed up the simulation results as well: measured cutoff frequency, gain, and phase response tracked the LTspice predictions closely, and the absolute THD deviation came in at just 0.04%. Taken together, these results point to a PINN-assisted Bayesian Optimization framework that is efficient, scalable, and well suited to next-generation computer-aided design of analog and mixed-signal circuits.

candidates.title: TempFit: Panoptic Symbol Spotting via Template Fitting
candidates.abstract: In this paper, we introduce TempFit , a novel approach for the problem of Panoptic Symbol Spotting on CAD drawings. Existing methods treat symbol spotting as a per-primitive classification or mask-prediction task, with no explicit constraint enforcing that the primitives assigned to one instance form a spatially connected group. As a result, predictions may erroneously merge primitives from distant symbols into a single instance or fragment a coherent symbol across multiple predictions. Motivated by the professional "retrieve-and-transform" CAD design workflow, we reformulate this task as a Template Fitting problem, where each foreground instance is detected by retrieving and aligning a canonical template from a library, enforcing structural completeness by construction. Building on this formulation, we present an autoregressive transformer that unifies template retrieval and pose prediction within a single end-to-end pipeline. The framework treats the template library as an explicit geometric memory, parsing background regions in parallel via learnable background tokens and synthesizing foreground instances autoregressively while attending to template-specific geometry at each step. Experiments on FloorplanCAD and our newly collected IndustryCAD dataset, a more challenging benchmark with complex industrial symbols, heavy occlusion, and wide scale variation, demonstrate state-of-the-art performance with particularly large gains on IndustryCAD. Project page: https://tempfit-project.github.io/.

candidates.title: Neural Centroidal Voronoi Tessellations
candidates.abstract: Centroidal Voronoi tessellation (CVT) is a fundamental primitive for high-quality surface sampling and isotropic remeshing in computer graphics. However, computing surface CVTs with classical solvers remains expensive: each optimization step repeatedly constructs restricted Voronoi diagrams (RVDs) and integrates quantities over their surface cells. We introduce Neural CVT , a learning-based surface-CVT solver that replaces these costly geometric computations with a recurrent neural optimizer, accelerating CVT optimization by one to two orders of magnitude in our benchmarks while preserving geometric fidelity. Given an input surface, we sample a dense point cloud and extract multi-scale geometric descriptors with a graph neural encoder. A lightweight recurrent optimizer then refines seed positions over a small number of iterations, aggregating interpolated surface features and optimization history to predict per-seed displacements. The framework is trained self-supervised using CVT objectives that promote uniform distributions and, when desired, feature alignment. Across diverse organic and CAD-like shapes, Neural CVT generalizes to unseen geometry, initialization strategies, and seed densities, producing isotropic, feature-preserving remeshes comparable to state-of-the-art offline optimization methods at a fraction of the computational cost. The code and trained models are available at https://github.com/sig-pku/NeuralCVT.

candidates.title: Does Machine Learning Beat ARIMA in Foreign Exchange? Out-of- Sample Evidence on Trading Activity, Volatility and Prices for EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/CAD, 2010–2021
candidates.abstract: Abstract Machine-learning models are used more and more to predict financial markets, but whether they beat simple time-series models is rarely tested under strict out-of-sample conditions. This study compares a Random Forest and a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM), each using 26 price-derived indicators, with ARIMA models and simple rules for EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/CAD, using daily data from 2010 to 2021 and an 890-day test period from February 2018 to July 2021. For next-day tick-volume activity the comparison depends on information. Without volume history the Random Forest correctly classifies 31.8–41.6% of test days, while ARIMA correctly classifies 61.5–63.8%; with volume history the difference between the two is not significant. The GBM forecasts five-day realised volatility less accurately than ARIMA for EUR/USD and USD/CAD and is not significantly different from it for GBP/USD. In the main design it beats a trailing-volatility baseline only for GBP/USD, where a constant forecast performs just as well. For the price, ARIMA does no better than the random walk. Seven robustness analyses, including GARCH and HAR benchmarks, yearly re-fits, a single data source and other horizons, leave these results unchanged. Of 114 tests, four machine-learning wins remain significant after the Holm correction, and all of them are against naive baselines. The results suggest that a price-based machine-learning forecast should beat a simple time-series model, on the same information and test days, before it is trusted. The code, a pinned data download and file hashes are released for reproduction. JEL Classification: C45; C52; C53; F31; G17

candidates.title: GOPR-CAD: Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating accurate CAD models requires substantial engineering expertise and careful control of geometry, topology, and mechanical constraints. Text-to-CAD aims to simplify this process, but current LLM-based methods often generate CAD programs directly. Language models remain unreliable when producing long code while coordinating coupled geometric, topological, and dimensional constraints. Consequently, executable programs may still produce structurally incorrect models, which execution rate and rendered appearance may fail to reveal. To address these limitations, we propose GOPR-CAD, an agentic Text-to-CAD pipeline based on Graph-of-Operations Progressive Reasoning. A language model acts as a decision agent over encapsulated CAD operations and progressively constructs an executable operation graph, which a deterministic compiler converts into the final CAD model. This separation requires no additional training and supports different language models. To evaluate structural fidelity, we construct MHCAD, a benchmark of 300 standard mechanical part requirements derived from Machinery's Handbook. Their explicit structures enable reference-free STEP/B-rep evaluation. GOPR-CAD achieves 82.7% Structural Yield on MHCAD, and 87.2% Structural Yield on an external CADPrompt subset.

candidates.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
candidates.abstract: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.

candidates.title: PhyCAD: Physics-Aware Text-to-CAD Generation via Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Language-driven computer-aided design (CAD) generation enables the creation of editable parametric models from text, yet geometric correctness alone does not ensure physical feasibility. We present PhyCAD, a framework for physics-aware Text-to-CAD generation that trains language models to produce executable CadQuery programs under geometric and physical constraints. To support this setting, we construct a Text-to-CAD dataset that links parametric CAD models with geometric specifications, loading conditions, and physical constraints. We further develop an automated CAD--CAE verifier that combines program execution, geometric checks, and finite element analysis to provide feedback for model training. A key learning challenge is to prioritize joint satisfaction of geometric and physical constraints while retaining informative feedback on partial progress. A flat aggregation of heterogeneous rewards can obscure this priority, allowing improvements in individual criteria to compensate for unmet design requirements. We therefore introduce a Hierarchical Balanced Advantage for Group Relative Policy Optimization, grouping candidates into levels according to their verification status and combining between-level progress with objective-wise peer ranking within each level. This formulation preserves cross-level priority in the training signal while providing fine-grained feedback for satisfying constraints and improving feasible designs. Experiments across multiple language models show that PhyCAD consistently improves joint geometric and physical constraint satisfaction. These results demonstrate the value of verifiable engineering feedback for advancing language-driven CAD generation beyond geometric reconstruction toward physics-aware design.

candidates.title: PrimitiveCAD: An LLM-Based Point-to-CAD Reconstruction with Primitive-Aware Tokenization and Operation Alignment
candidates.abstract: Large-model-based point-to-CAD generation holds immense potential for advancing industrial design and enhancing 3D modeling efficiency. However, most existing methods approach the problem as a general point-cloud encoding and token prediction task, neglecting the tokenization and supervision specifically for CAD-related primitives. As a result, these methods often struggle to accurately reconstruct the intricate primitive structures. To address this limitation, we propose PrimitiveCAD, a novel multi-stage paradigm for point-to-CAD reconstruction that enhances the geometric accuracy of generated CAD models while better preserving critical geometric features. First, we introduce a primitive-aware point cloud tokenization model, enabling the system to learn more robust geometric representations from CAD point clouds. Next, we perform supervised finetuning on a large language model (LLM) and introduce an operation alignment loss to align key CAD operation frequencies, thereby improving the preservation of global shape features. Finally, we incorporate reinforcement learning (RL) and introduce a feature-line alignment reward to further reduce stochasticity and enhance the fine-grained preservation of geometric features. Experiments on the DeepCAD and Fusion360 datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in code validity, geometric accuracy, and geometric feature preservation.

candidates.title: Done Is Not Correct: Measuring Silent Failures and Self-Verification Calibration When LLM Agents Take CAD Actions
candidates.abstract: When a large language model (LLM) agent writes parametric CAD code from a natural-language specification, syntactic success decouples from semantic correctness. We release a benchmark and harness that measure this gap directly: 13 specification tasks whose every requirement maps to machine-checkable properties of the produced B-rep, measured by the kernel against published tolerance bands, with reference solutions and the full graded attempt corpus. The exact, self-audited oracle isolates two quantities no prior CAD benchmark reports: the silent-failure rate (a valid, renderable solid, an explicit completion claim, and at least one failed semantic check) and completion-claim calibration. Across four models from four vendors (156 attempts per architecture), single-shot agents claimed completion on 98% of attempts and were silently wrong on 14.1%; a tool-use loop that enforces measure-then-claim cut silent failures to 3.2% and raised claim precision from 64% to 96%, and a four-model ablation attributes the change to the claim contract rather than the feedback. A planner-coder-checker pipeline matched that precision at lower coverage with no success gain. Stated confidence was miscalibrated single-shot (ECE 0.32) and became informative under verification for three of four models. Hardening our own oracle flipped 18 of 519 regraded verdicts from pass to fail and none in reverse; a blind expert audit overturned 3 of the 18 silent failures outside the one ambiguously specified task; and fourfold scaling of every tolerance band leaves the contrast intact.

candidates.title: Multimodality noninvasive imaging in the evaluation of coronary artery disease: a narrative review
candidates.abstract: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and its evaluation has evolved beyond the identification of obstructive epicardial stenosis alone. Contemporary imaging increasingly emphasizes an integrated assessment of coronary anatomy, plaque burden and composition, lesion-specific ischemia, myocardial viability, scar, ventricular remodeling, and coronary microvascular dysfunction. Anatomic and functional imaging provide complementary information regarding coronary atherosclerosis, lesion-specific physiology, inducible ischemia, myocardial blood flow, viability, scar, and microvascular disease, with test selection guided by the clinical question and patient characteristics. Randomized trials of specific imaging-guided strategies have demonstrated differences in diagnostic efficiency, downstream invasive angiography, preventive therapy, revascularization, and procedural complications. In contrast, effects on symptoms and hard cardiovascular outcomes vary according to the population, comparator, and duration of follow-up. Emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, radiomics, photon-counting computed tomography, molecular imaging, and hybrid imaging, are at different stages of clinical readiness and require varying degrees of further validation before routine implementation. This review summarizes the current role, evidence base, limitations, and future directions of multimodality noninvasive imaging in CAD, providing a practical framework for selecting the appropriate test according to the clinical question and patient profile.

candidates.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD, a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that ''renders'' node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.

candidates.title: TerraFuture Omega v20: Universal Recoverability-Constrained Engineering, Safety, Human Rights and Living Continuity Architecture
candidates.abstract: TerraFuture Omega v20 is an integrated, cross-domain research and engineering architecture designed to explore how machines, materials, intelligent systems, infrastructure, transport, essential services and institutional processes can be developed around human rights, technical safety, collaboration, care, help, empathy, compassion, recoverability and continuity. The archive brings together twenty cumulative development editions covering conceptual machinery, engineering drawings, parametric CAD models, software reference implementations, safety and recovery mechanisms, renewable-energy configurations, advanced materials, regenerative and self-repair concepts, intelligent sensors, protective switches, human-machine collaboration, emergency response, global challenges, alliance structures and evidence-constrained governance. Its central proposition is that technological advancement should not be assessed solely by performance, autonomy, efficiency or computational capability. It should also be assessed by the protection of people, prevention of foreseeable harm, accessibility, accountability, continuity of essential functions, independent verification and preservation of recoverable future options. 1. Foundational research architecture The project applies Recoverability-Constrained Systems and Continuity Science principles across engineering, software, governance and service-continuity contexts. Core principles include: Protection of life, dignity and fundamental human rights. Collaboration, care, help, empathy and compassion. Prevention and reduction of foreseeable harm. Independent safety controls and accountable human oversight. Evidence-based decisions and explicit treatment of uncertainty. Safe interruption, isolation, recovery and authorized restart. Accessibility, non-discrimination, participation and remedies. Traceable system identity, verification and auditability. Preservation of essential services during disruption. Responsible regeneration, reconstruction and future adaptation. The architecture incorporates finite design catalogs and expandable combination grammars, allowing research proposals to be explored systematically without treating conceptual possibilities as demonstrated technologies. 2. Machine and product innovation The archive includes conceptual product and machine families for ergonomic earth-moving equipment, electric and solar-powered tools, assisted machinery, regenerative devices, transport protection and industrial automation. Proposed technical developments include: Ergonomic and electrically assisted excavation equipment. Solar charging and modular energy systems. Exoskeleton-assisted and robotic work systems. Vehicle and powered-door injury prevention. Rail, aviation, marine and industrial safety instruments. Overheating, overcurrent, overload and fault-detection switches. Self-monitoring and modularly repairable machinery. Self-healing materials and bio-inspired engineering concepts. Water, energy, environmental and disaster-response instruments. Accessibility and assistive technologies. Sensors, instrumentation and human-supervised AI systems. The archive contains reference CAD, mesh, drawing, specification and testing materials. These constitute research and prototype-development inputs rather than approved production designs. 3. Safety and recoverability architecture The proposed safety model combines hazard identification, protective sensing, independent interlocks, operational constraints, controlled stopping, fault isolation, human intervention, repair verification and accountable authorization. Artificial intelligence is treated as a potential advisory, diagnostic and optimization layer, not as an inherently sufficient authority for safety-critical action. Different machines require different protective responses. An immediate electrical shutdown may be appropriate in one system, while another may require controlled braking, load holding, containment, cooling or continued backup operation. Return to service is conditioned on relevant evidence and authorization rather than the mere disappearance of a fault indication. 4. Human rights, care and institutional safeguards Human rights are proposed as foundational design and review requirements throughout the archive. The governance layer addresses dignity, equality, accessibility, consent, child protection, dependent-person safeguards, participation, privacy, fair treatment and effective remedies. Collaboration, care, help, empathy and compassion provide an additional human-centered review framework for machines, organizations, services, decisions and institutional responses. The archive distinguishes internationally recognized legal protections from newly proposed engineering or governance principles. Legal applicability depends on jurisdiction, context and relevant instruments. 5. Global challenges and continuity The project explores potential interventions concerning healthcare, water, sanitation, food systems, energy, construction, transport, environmental hazards, climate adaptation, education, digital infrastructure, emergency management and institutional accountability. Proposed systems are organized around prevention, normal operation, early warning, safe degradation, emergency response, recovery, reconstruction and future renewal. The architecture also explores collaboration among communities, researchers, manufacturers, public institutions, professional services and humanitarian organizations. Such relationships are proposals, not representations of existing agreements. 6. Executable reference software and verification Version 20 introduces additional evidence-constrained software tools, an accountable gap-closure queue, prioritized engineering concepts, foundational release gates, adversarial scenarios, audit-chain demonstrations and technical review workflows. The archive contains Python reference implementations and associated automated tests, together with research catalogs, safety records, specifications and cross-domain traceability documents. In the v20 development checks, 21 new automated reference tests passed. These tests assess limited software and documentation behavior. They do not establish physical-machine safety, scientific proof of novel mechanisms, legal compliance or successful deployment. The archive retains 540 inherited gap and action records requiring further review. Their presence should not be interpreted as 540 independently verified physical defects or as completed remediation. 7. Living research system TerraFuture Omega incorporates finite catalogs, deterministic design exploration, conceptual technology combinations, version tracking, evidence requirements and open-ended research procedures. A finite design space may be enumerated when its assumptions and boundaries are explicitly specified. Future discoveries, changing conditions and unknown hazards cannot be exhaustively resolved by any static archive. New proposals must therefore remain distinguishable from validated results. The living-system model supports revision, challenge, rejection, revalidation and responsible continuation. 8. Research limitations TerraFuture Omega v20 is a conceptual engineering, computational research and governance reference archive. The archive does not claim: Certification of physical machinery or protective devices. Completed field trials for the proposed machines. Proven prevention of injuries or global system failures. Independent validation of every generated combination. Regulatory authorization for transport or medical applications. Establishment of new binding international law. Patentability or exclusive novelty of all proposed technologies. Exhaustion of all possible scientific discoveries or future design paths. Manufacturing, installation, deployment and safety-critical operation require qualified engineering, appropriate testing, applicable legal review and independent authorization. 9. Intended users and applications The archive is intended for researchers, engineers, educators, manufacturers, safety specialists, accessibility professionals, public-interest technology developers, humanitarian planners, policy analysts and interdisciplinary research teams. Potential applications include research planning, prototype specifications, hazard analysis, requirements engineering, design-space exploration, educational demonstrations, evidence management and continuity assessment. 10. Conclusion TerraFuture Omega v20 proposes a unified approach in which innovation remains accountable to people, safety, evidence and recoverability. Its foundational objective is to design systems that anticipate hazards, protect affected beings, maintain essential functions, respond compassionately to failures, verify recovery and remain adaptable to future knowledge. The research framework adopts a non-circular stopping principle: verified results remain distinct from conceptual proposals, unresolved conditions remain visible, and new evidence may reopen the development process. Publication status: Research and reference-software release. Physical engineering and operational validation remain outstanding.

candidates.title: Prediction of Deep Neural Network for TCAD Analysis of Degradation Induced by Near-Interface Displacement Defects in 4H-SiC MOSFETs
candidates.abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) devices used in space and nuclear environments are exposed to radiation that creates displacement defects (DDs), but the effect of DDs near the gate oxide/SiC interface has not been analyzed systematically. Using technology computer-aided design (TCAD) simulation, this study analyzes how near-interface DDs in a 4H-SiC metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor (MOSFET) affect the threshold voltage (Vth), transconductance (gm), and on-current (Ion), and builds deep neural network (DNN) models that predict these effects. The DDs were modeled as acceptor-like traps with varied energy levels, concentration, depth, lateral position, and distribution width. The degradation was largest at the channel entrance and the edge of the junction field-effect transistor (JFET) region. The center depth mattered little while the trap region reached the interface, whereas a small gap between the trap region and the interface strongly reduced the degradation. Shallow-level traps reduced Ion without shifting Vth, whereas only deep-level traps caused an actual Vth shift. The DNNs accurately predicted the degradation for new TCAD conditions in which the trap parameters simultaneously took values not used in training and outperformed grid interpolation and other regression models. The trained DNNs thus rapidly predict the degradation at the simulated lateral positions for radiation reliability assessment.

candidates.title: Comparative evaluation of neural network models for geometric deviation prediction and toolpath compensation in double-sided incremental forming
candidates.abstract: Double-sided incremental forming (DSIF) is a dieless sheet metal forming process suitable for low-volume production but is limited by springback-induced geometric deviation. In this work, machine learning is used to predict the geometric deviation of a formed part. Then, these values are applied to the initial computer-aided design (CAD) model as toolpath compensation to provide a cost-effective approach to improve the accuracy of the final part compared to the target geometry after unclamping and springback. Three neural network models, i.e., a feedforward artificial neural network (ANN), a convolutional neural network (CNN), and a graph neural network (GNN), are trained on a unified experimental dataset with deep drawing quality (DDQ) steel as the material formed and directly compared for geometric deviation prediction and accuracy after toolpath compensation. The dataset is generated by forming 25 parts with diverse geometries and measuring their post-unclamping geometric deviations. Although model-specific preprocessing is required, all neural network models use consistent local geometric input features, e.g., spatial coordinates and surface normal components, and the corresponding measured geometric deviation as the output. Two unseen geometries are used for evaluation. The ANN, CNN, and GNN models achieve average prediction mean absolute errors of 0.45, 0.32, and 0.41 mm, respectively, on the two unseen geometries. The predicted deviations are then used to create modified CAD models, reducing the geometric deviation by 34%, 49%, and 51% for ANN-, CNN-, and GNN-based compensation, respectively. This study shows that neural network models with explicit spatial information aggregation, i.e., CNN and GNN models, outperform the ANN model in improving the geometric accuracy of DSIF.

candidates.title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of airway nodules on CT for early medical intervention
candidates.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Airway lesions are common CT findings in interval and post-screen lung cancers; however, airway nodules are frequently overlooked. Robust artificial intelligence (AI) tools for characterizing airway nodules remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models for the detection and classification of airway nodules on low-dose CT(LDCT) as a second-reading tool. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 1813 segmental and more proximal airway nodules were retrospectively identified from 1107 LDCT of 1043 participants. A sphere-based center-points matching network, first used to establish a lung nodule detection model, was transferred to airway nodules and enhanced by incorporating coordinate and multiscale attention. The model was trained on 907 proximal airway nodules and independently tested on 738 proximal nodules across four hospitals. The clinical utility of the AI tool was evaluated through human-AI interaction. For nodule classification, a 3D SEResNeXt101-based model was trained, validated and tested using 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) with a 6:2:2 split and evaluated in an independent testing dataset. RESULTS: On the independent testing set, the detection model achieved a high sensitivity of 73.7%. Human-AI interaction demonstrated AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' performance, increasing sensitivity from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1-score from 49.4% to 77.2%, while reducing diagnosis time from 83.8 s to 61.8 s. The classification model showed high sensitivities of 82.1%, 71.4%, 94.3%, 72.7% and specificities of 62.7%, 73.9%, 73.9%, 87.5% across multicenter training, validation, testing and independent testing sets, respectively. CONCLUSION: This AI system significantly enhances the detection and classification of proximal airway nodules, guiding early medical intervention. KEY POINTS: Question Improved early detection and classification of airway nodules are critical for lung cancer mortality reduction, but AI-based CAD systems targeting airway nodules remain scarce. Findings The DL models for detection and classification of proximal airway nodules on chest CT were developed and assisted radiologists to achieve higher detection accuracy. Critical Relevance Statement The clinical applications of the proposed DL-based system for detecting and classifying proximal airway nodules on chest CT scans help radiologists reduce missed/delayed diagnoses and shorten diagnostic time as a second-reading tool, guiding medical intervention and improving clinical outcomes.

candidates.title: Advancements in Artificial Intelligence for Enhanced Diagnosis and Prognosis in Cardiac CT: a Comprehensive Review and Future Perspectives
candidates.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Cardiovascular disease, with coronary artery disease (CAD) as its main culprit, remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Traditional diagnostic methods that focus on the degree of arterial narrowing (percent diameter stenosis, or %DS) can miss early signs of disease or the specific plaque features that indicate high risk. The purpose of this review is to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can enhance the diagnostic and prognostic capabilities of cardiac computed tomography (CCT), and to address where AI can most meaningfully improve diagnostic accuracy, workflow efficiency, and patient care. RECENT FINDINGS: AI is transforming cardiac CT across the entire imaging pathway. By applying AI algorithms, recent studies have refined the assessment of coronary artery calcium (CAC), improved plaque characterization, and detected subtle lesions that might evade traditional detection methods. AI further enables non-invasive assessment of ischemia (reduced blood flow), aids in the evaluation of myocardial infarction, analyzes adipose tissue surrounding the heart, improves image quality, and provides valuable prognostic insights for risk stratification. This comprehensive review explores the transformative potential of AI in cardiac CT, highlighting its role in accurate diagnosis, precise risk stratification, and personalized management of cardiovascular disease. Through collaboration between AI technology and clinical expertise, we envision a future where cardiac CT imaging is more powerful, efficient, and patient-centered, ultimately leading to improved outcomes in cardiovascular medicine. Continued standardization, external validation, and clinician education will be essential to realize this impact in routine practice.

candidates.title: SO(3)-Equivariant Learning on CAD Boundary Representations
candidates.abstract: Learning on boundary representations (B-reps) requires robustness to the pose of a part, since CAD models are not stored in a canonical orientation. Existing B-rep networks either operate on world-frame coordinates and normals, and thus degrade under rotation, or encode each face in a local reference frame. Local frames yield invariance, but reduce inter-face messages to scalars and discard the relative orientation of adjacent faces. We propose SO3brep, an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network on the B-rep face-adjacency graph. Node features are computed in local frames and mapped into a shared frame by Wigner D-matrices. Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple these features with the directions between adjacent faces, so that relative orientation is preserved throughout message passing and the output remains SE(3)-invariant. Across three face-segmentation and two classification benchmarks with randomly rotated test parts, SO3brep achieves the highest accuracy among the compared B-rep networks and equivariant point cloud networks, with the fewest parameters. Its advantage is largest with few labeled parts, a setting typical of industrial CAD. Code is available at https://github.com/UGent-CVAMO/so3brep.

We propose SO3brep, an SO(3)-equivariant graph neural network on the B-rep face-adjacency graph. Node features are computed in local frames and mapped into a shared frame by Wigner D-matrices. Clebsch-Gordan tensor products couple these features with the directions between adjacent faces, so that relative orientation is preserved throughout message passing and the output remains SE(3)-invariant. Across three face-segmentation and two classification benchmarks with randomly rotated test parts, SO3brep achieves the highest accuracy among the compared B-rep networks and equivariant point cloud networks, with the fewest parameters. Its advantage is largest with few labeled parts, a setting typical of industrial CAD. Code is available at https://github.com/UGent-CVAMO/so3brep.

candidates.title: Mechanical Engineering Skills: An Open Library of Agent Skills for Design, Analysis and Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Mechanical engineers use specialized tools for CAD, simulation, manufacturing and research, each with a distinct interface and learning curve. We present Mechanical Engineering Skills, an open library of 33 agent skills that makes these capabilities accessible through a single text or voice conversation. Each skill combines operating instructions, executable tools and verification procedures. A language model interprets the request, selects and coordinates skills, while deterministic tools perform computations and return checked results. Default workflows require no tool-specific interface training, local model execution or model fine-tuning; skills load on demand and install with one command. Nineteen skills adapt published or preprint research from our laboratory, including text-to-CAD, linkage synthesis, CFD setup, stress-field and lattice surrogates, equation discovery, additive-manufacturing planning and in-process monitoring. Fourteen additional skills support core engineering and education. We describe the skill format, design principles and a method for translating research into practical workflows. Five case studies with explicit evidence scopes and independent reruns demonstrate exact analytical agreement for lattice homogenization, rocket apogee predictions within 4% of stored OpenRocket references, an equation fit nine times more accurate than a cubic polynomial at an unseen temperature, and an end-to-end rehearsal of porosity monitoring. Controlled agent comparisons remain future work. The open library is available at https://github.com/BaratiLab/mechanical-engineering-skills.

candidates.title: Influence of geometric-process representation explicitness on transformer-based NC code generation
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generating numerical control (NC) code from computer-aided design (CAD) models is one of the most knowledge-intensive tasks in digital manufacturing, yet how explicit the input representation should be has received little empirical attention. This study encodes the same machining cases at three levels of increasing explicitness — geometry only (L1), geometry with a tool library (L2), and geometry with both a tool library and an operation-level process plan (L3) — on a deterministic dataset of 9,000 prismatic workpieces, fine-tunes a CodeT5 + 220 M encoder–decoder for each level under five training seeds, and evaluates 900 held-out cases through a hierarchical five-level framework from syntax to geometric correspondence. Explicitness had no robust effect on single-sample correctness: mean geometric-correspondence pass rates were 0.954, 0.952, and 0.969 for L1, L2, and L3, a spread an order of magnitude smaller than the between-seed range, and the L1–L3 contrast was significant in opposite directions under two seeds. Its effect on reproducibility was consistent: the geometric reproducibility of L3 stayed at 0.95 or above under every seed and every decoding temperature up to 0.8, whereas L1 and L2 matched it under four seeds and collapsed to about 0.55 under the fifth. An explicitness index counting the process decisions a representation supplies rather than leaves to be inferred reproduces this pattern quantitatively, and a deterministic rule-based reference shows that the omitted decisions can equally be supplied by process-planning rules. Explicitness therefore acts primarily as a stabiliser of reproducibility rather than as a means of improving single-program correctness.

candidates.title: Parametric CAD Bench v3: Evaluating Agentic Parametric CAD Authoring from Text and Engineering Drawings
candidates.abstract: Producing an executable CAD script is not sufficient to establish that an agent has satisfied an engineering design request. Evaluation must also consider the resulting geometry, specified dimensions, and native CAD modeling history. We present Parametric CAD Bench v3, a 100-task benchmark comprising 30 text-to-CAD creation tasks, 30 text-to-CAD create-and-edit tasks, and 40 tasks that reconstruct mechanical parts from engineering drawings. Agents operate in a pinned FreeCAD environment and submit native CAD artifacts to a separate programmatic verifier. The primary metric is mean continuous task reward, combining geometry similarity and specification consistency rather than binary task success. A September 24, 2026 snapshot covers 13 model-agent systems; Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 achieves the highest overall point estimate, 61.03%, and an image-to-CAD mean reward of 84.66%. These measurements describe complete systems, not isolated model capabilities. We release versioned tasks, evaluation configurations, and inspectable result artifacts.

candidates.title: Physics-aware calibration neural network for automated TCAD-to-experiment modeling of carbon nanotube field-effect transistors
candidates.abstract: Abstract Low-dimensional semiconductor devices, including carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNT-FETs), require efficient calibration methods to reconcile numerical simulations with experimentally measured electrical characteristics. Conventional manual calibration is time-consuming, while purely data-driven surrogate models may provide limited physical interpretability and reduced reliability when applied to device geometries outside the training domain. In this work, we propose a physics-aware calibration neural network (PACNN) for supervised technology computer-aided design (TCAD)-to-experiment calibration of CNT-FET transfer and output characteristics. PACNN uses current–voltage curves generated by a two-dimensional intrinsic silicon TCAD model as a stable numerical reference. The architecture combines an anchor-preserving physical-affine module, which accounts for global variations in voltage alignment, current amplitude, slope, and extracted electrical parameters, with family-specific bounded residual modules that correct the remaining local discrepancies. Transfer characteristics are processed in the signed logarithmic current domain, whereas output characteristics are calibrated in the normalized linear current domain using separate amplitude and low-rank shape corrections. Model training incorporates curve-fitting, curve-level R 2 , slope consistency, device parameter, residual, and regularization objectives. Channel-length generalization was evaluated through out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation to $${L}_\mathrm{ch}$$ L ch = 4.5 μm and 5.0 μm. PACNN achieved macro-averaged curve-wise R 2 values of 0.947 4 and 0.876 0 for the transfer and output characteristics, respectively, with corresponding pooled pointwise R 2 values of 0.962 7 and 0.996 2. The predicted curves also preserved key electrical parameters, yielding a balanced physical consistency index of 0.918 3. These results indicate that PACNN provides an accurate and physically constrained framework for automated TCAD-to-experiment calibration of CNT-FET characteristics.

candidates.title: PixelBench: Can LLMs Understand and Generate Images Pixel by Pixel?
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate visual assets through text-based formats such as SVG and CAD, but these symbolic representations describe images using high-level primitives rather than explicit raster values. We ask whether LLMs can instead generate pixel images directly through their existing vocabulary, without a learned image tokenizer or decoder. We introduce PixelBench, a benchmark for text-to-pixel (T2P) and image-to-pixel (I2P) generation across multiple resolutions, together with a complementary pixel-understanding evaluation. Models generate an RGB color palette followed by a grid of indices specifying the palette color of each output pixel. In T2P, the strongest models produce recognizable images directly from text. In I2P, the strongest models outperform palette-matched downsampling and specialized pixelization algorithms at low resolutions. Pixel-understanding performance correlates strongly with generation performance. A resolution-scaling study shows that pixel-generation performance often improves initially before declining at high resolutions. Finally, we introduce Pixel Reconstruction Tuning (PRT), which augments visual instruction tuning with caption-palette-grid trajectories. We post-train Molmo2-4B from its pretraining checkpoint by mixing general instruction data with our curated PRT data, improving performance across 16 visual-centric benchmarks, indicating that explicit pixel reconstruction can provide useful auxiliary supervision.

candidates.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
candidates.abstract: Rapid advances in cowork agents are shifting human-AI collaboration toward real-world automation, delivering software, designs, and other artifacts. However, such productivity work demands both high-quality delivery on complex productivity tasks and continued monitoring and decision-making over long horizons, a combination that remains an open challenge. We introduce CoworkOS, a general-purpose harness for long-horizon work that separates task strategy from execution management: the model decides actions, delegation, and acceptance, while the runtime maintains state and feedback. Its three-layer architecture enables direct execution or delegation to Subagents, synchronously or asynchronously, under stable responsibilities. Through a shared application layer, humans and agents inspect and revise the same evolving documents, presentations, CAD models, and Blender scenes, so human-in-the-loop participation can enter both through conversation and through direct modification of the work itself. To sustain continuity across agents and sessions, CoworkOS further introduces hierarchical workspaces and persistent semantic memory, so working files, key decisions, and long-running Job logs remain shareable, reusable, and resumable after interruption. Across 12 benchmarks and 6 categories of real-world applications, CoworkOS proves highly competitive with frontier agent applications such as Codex and DeepSeek Harness. As a sustained-work case study, CoworkOS uses GLM-5.3 as its backbone to conduct RSI-driven automated post-training on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Over five rounds, the model's average score across eight benchmarks rose from 33.19 to 42.95 (+9.76). Looking ahead, we believe CoworkOS opens a meaningful path toward general cowork-agent intelligence.

candidates.title: Blueprint2CAD: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Engineering Drawing-to-CAD Render Correspondence
candidates.abstract: Engineering drawings specify mechanical parts through orthographic projections. Recognizing which part a drawing depicts underlies part search, design reuse, and digitization, yet no public benchmark measures whether vision models can do it. We introduce Blueprint2CAD, a benchmark for drawing-to-render correspondence: given an orthographic line drawing and a shaded render, usually from another viewpoint, decide whether they show the same part. Its data layer, BlueCAD-30K, applies an open drafting pipeline to 29,925 Zero-to-CAD models, adding view-aligned renders, clean and dimensioned drawings from six viewpoints, and surface-type metadata. Frozen encoders retrieve the matching part from a 10,000-model gallery with up to 65% Recall@1 when viewpoints are known but 43% when they are not, and the four encoders we test lie within six points of each other: viewpoint, not backbone, is the bottleneck. Six zero-shot vision-language models reach only 0.52-0.67 verification accuracy, with model-specific Yes/No biases that chain-of-thought shifts but does not remove; a quick LoRA fine-tuning on in-domain pairs improves verification accuracy by a few points but sharpens these biases and leaves the viewpoint failure intact.

candidates.title: Abstract 6313: Integration of Genomic and Lab Data with Dynamic EHR Modeling
candidates.abstract: Background: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) for cardiovascular disease are almost always used as static covariates in proportional-hazards (PH) models - a single number, fixed for life. However, genetic effects on coronary artery disease (CAD) and other CV outcomes are non-stationary, rising and falling with age; when genetic risk inflects reshapes prevention timing and within-phenotype heterogeneity. We reshape Aladynoulli, an interpretable Bayesian generative model that simultaneously discovers latent disease structure and predicts individual trajectories from the longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) and genome, by allowing age-varying genetic effects (gamma_slope) to accommodate non-proportional hazards, and jointly integrating cardiometabolic-lab integration. Methods: We trained Aladynoulli on longitudinal records of 400,000 UK Biobank (UKB) and 53,000 Mass General Brigham (MGB) participants, jointly modeling 348 disease phecodes and 40 routine labs across ages 30-80. For each of 21 latent disease signatures we learned a level (gamma_level) and age-velocity (gamma_slope) coefficient on each of 36 PRS, letting effects evolve with age. Prospective 1-year prediction used leave-one-batch-out cross-validation (40 batches; disjoint train/test), benchmarked against the no-slope model on identical folds. Results: gamma_slope captured non-proportional hazards in 9/10 CV disease-PRS pairs. For CAD, the observed Q4-vs-Q1 PRS hazard ratio fell from 7.1 at age 45 to 2.5 at age 70 (-0.18/yr); the slope model recovered this decline while the static model predicted a flat HR. The same age-attenuation held for atrial fibrillation (AF) and type 1 diabetes. The slope model improved 1-year prediction in 27/28 diseases (mean +0.10 AUC), with the largest CV gains (AUC, bootstrap 95% CI): ASCVD 0.925->0.980 (0.976-0.983), AF 0.907->0.985 (0.974-0.991), heart failure 0.886->0.980 (0.968-0.992), stroke 0.754->0.899 (0.858-0.936). Crucially, the same model is a discovery engine: it learned all 21 comorbidity signatures and their PRS drivers de novo, recovered established CAD, AF, and diabetes genetic associations, newly localized the age at which each genetic effect peaks, and the signatures replicated across UKB and MGB. Joint lab modeling in MGB further discovered cardiometabolic subtypes - LDL/cholesterol within the ischemic signature, glucose/HbA1c within the diabetes/hypertension signature. Conclusions: Modeling CV polygenic risk as time-varying rather than static lets a single interpretable model discover disease structure and predict individual trajectories at once - substantially improving 1-year prediction and recovering the age-attenuation that PH methods miss. Aladynoulli's interpretable structure allows it to uniquely capture the interaction between time and genomics unlike black-box EHR foundation models.

candidates.title: Inclusive Restaurant Acoustics for Visually Impaired Users: Exploring Parametric Potential
candidates.abstract: In the current context of performance - based design, parametric design offers the opportunity to integrate acoustic criteria from the early stages of architectural conception. This paper investigates the role of sound - absorbing panels and walls with parametric structures in optimizing the acoustic environment of restaurants, with a particular focus on improving the experience of people with visual impairments. In Romania, approximately 90,000 people live with visual impairments, and their participation in social life and everyday activities such as dining out is often affected by the uncontrolled acoustic performance of interior spaces — an aspect that is rarely addressed systematically in traditional design practices. In dining and social spaces characterized by high levels of ambient noise and increased reverberation time, auditory clarity becomes essential for spatial orientation, social interaction, and the reduction of cognitive overload. For users with visual impairments, auditory perception represents a fundamental tool for navigating and interpreting space, which transforms acoustic control into a critical component of inclusive design. In addition to using ambient sounds and voices for orientation, many individuals rely on active and passive echolocation mechanisms. By analyzing subtle differences between direct and reflected sound, users can estimate the distance to obstacles, the size of the interior volume, or the openness of a spatial area. A space with chaotic echoes or excessive diffuse noise can compromise orientation ability and the perception of spatial boundaries. The paper proposes a parametric approach to the design of sound - absorbing panels and walls, in which geometry, perforation density, relief depth, and the distribution of absorbing elements are generated and optimized algorithmically within digital environments integrated with acoustic simulation. Within this framework, parameters such as reverberation time, absorption coefficient, and sound field distribution become active design variables rather than mere post - design evaluation indicators. Thus, acoustic systems are conceived as adaptive structures capable of responding to spatial volume, materiality, and occupancy levels through variable three - dimensional configurations and perforated or textured surfaces with parametrically generated patterns that combine acoustic performance with formal expressiveness. The research methodology includes a qualitative research with semi - structured interviews and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis to demonstrate that the early integration of acoustic design significantly improves the visual impaired users while being in a restaurant. The results highlight the potential of parametric design to transform sound - absorbing panels and acoustic walls from technical elements added later in the process into generative components of the architectural concept. The study argues for the development of a practice of “parametric acoustics,” in which performance, inclusion, and formal expression are interconnected through advanced digital tools.

candidates.title: Trustworthy Execution of Industrial Agents
candidates.abstract: Industrial agents increasingly modify persistent engineering objects rather than merely generate answers. Authentication and successful calls cannot establish whether intended changes occurred, evidence supports a conclusion, or historical results remain applicable. We present a framework for trustworthy industrial-agent execution within a single enterprise governance domain. Eight control domains assign responsibilities across authority, planning, composition, tool execution, actual effects, evidence, baseline and use governance, and recovery and evolution. A four-plane architecture and three control chains connect these responsibilities through typed objects and version-bound interfaces. The specification separates tool returns from actual engineering effects, evidence coverage from engineering judgment, and historical lifecycle state from current applicability. Multi-agent handoffs are an architectural extension examined through deterministic interface tests. Distinct prototypes examine selected mechanisms using conformance tests, ablations, uncertainty stress, CAD/CAE execution, and local persistence. An OpenFOAM fixture produces COMPLETE coverage with FAIL judgment; an expired-job case requires readmission despite completed computation. CAD and recovery counterexamples expose omitted mandatory checks, discarded negative facts, and inconsistent producer-consumer mappings. Targeted repairs support local regression conclusions. The reported 0/29 hazardous commits measure closed-set specification conformance, not a safety probability. We distinguish the complete framework, implemented paths, and empirical evidence, identifying check-inventory completeness and cross-module fact preservation as prerequisites for extending these results.

candidates.title: Toward Agentic AI-Ready Workflows in Built Environment Organizations: Knowledge Structures and Interoperability Challenges
candidates.abstract: The rise of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) in the built environment is shifting attention from isolated AI tools toward autonomous systems that reason, plan, and act across project and organizational workflows. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on large language model capabilities, but also on the readiness of heterogeneous data environments across the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) sector. These environments combine structured sources, such as CAD and BIM models, schedules, cost databases, and asset registers, with unstructured ones, including technical reports, design narratives, planning and policy documents, contracts, meeting minutes, and risk registers. This paper reviews how built environment data can be organized to support agentic AI-ready workflows, focusing on knowledge structures, interoperability, and access and integration mechanisms such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Drawing on existing literature, it examines approaches proposed to organize structured and unstructured data and considers how such data can be contextualized and made accessible to AI agents in a reliable manner. The paper synthesizes current perspectives, highlights challenges around fragmentation and interoperability, and identifies open questions for future research on AI-compatible information management in the built environment.

candidates.title: Smart Morphodynamic Biomaterials: Multi‐Stimuli 4D ‐Printed Polymer Architectures for Autonomous and Next‐Generation Wound Repair
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Four‐dimensional (4D) printed polymer scaffolds are intelligent biomaterials that can revolutionize wound care by utilizing stimuli‐responsive polymers, programmable shape memory, and adaptive design to tackle the limitations imposed by static wound dressings and traditional 3D printed structures. This review describes an extensive analysis of the progress made from single stimulus‐responsive systems to dual‐ and multiple stimuli‐responsive systems that react to the changing wound environment. A comparative evaluation of stimulus platforms is presented through a proposed wound‐relevant performance framework covering the figure‐of‐merit (FoM) measurement, orthogonal hybrid stimulus design strategies, and translation needs for next‐generation wound devices. This paper also highlights CAD (Computer‐Aided Design), material intelligence, and advanced fabrication strategies to create next‐generation scaffolds that actively interact with biological tissues. Polymer chemistry and dynamic 4D functionality are integrated to create scaffolds that adhere to wound geometries, modify microenvironmental variables, and precisely distribute drugs. Recent pioneering ideas concerning the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are addressed, including how these methods can be used to overcome existing problems associated with 4D‐printed wound healing scaffolds. A roadmap is provided here that outlines the areas of research that should be explored to validate 4D printing of wound healing constructs. Together, these discoveries highlight the field's increasing proximity to clinical translation and place 4D polymer scaffolds as the future of intelligent wound care.

candidates.title: Research on cross-modal reconstruction of Li brocade 2D patterns to 3D structures based on the Pix2PixHD generative model
candidates.abstract: Li brocade, a textile heritage of the Li people inscribed by UNESCO for urgent safeguarding, survives largely as flat photographs, from which learning-based reconstruction tends to lose pattern detail and distort 3D form. This study reconstructs Li brocade garments from a single 2D pattern image. An improved Pix2PixHD with multiscale attention and an attention-weighted texture consistency loss synthesizes the texture, and a graph convolutional network predicts garment displacements on an SMPL body fitted to the wearer. An explicit garment category condition, kept separate from the pattern features, selects the base mesh, the deformation manifold, and the seam rules, which follow the assembly of Li brocade garments from narrow woven panels. The Li-Brocade3D dataset contains 13,256 samples, including a held-out test set of 428 real garments whose structured light scans serve as ground truth, with synthetic samples simulated in CLO3D with fabric parameters calibrated on woven swatches against measured drape. On the test set, the method reaches an FID of 24.78, an SSIM of 0.866, a Chamfer distance of 3.71 mm and an expert pattern integrity score of 87.8, reducing FID by 36.4% relative to Pix2PixHD and Chamfer distance by 37.3% relative to Neural Cloth. A category inferred from the pattern image alone is correct for only 91.6% of test samples, and a wrong category raises the Chamfer distance by 67.4%. On 40 specimens, a garment CAD workflow in CLO3D driven by measured pattern pieces is more accurate, 3.13 mm against 3.71 mm, but needs about 140 min of manual work per garment against 0.60 s. Perceptual experiments place the mean angular distortion of 2.88° below the detection threshold of lay observers and slightly above that of heritage professionals, whereas the distortion of headscarves stays visible to both and is the main limitation.

candidates.title: Digital Twin-Driven Generative Design of Multi-Layer Cultivation Systems for Vertical Farming with Solar Light
candidates.abstract: Multi-layer Cultivation Systems (MCSs) intensify urban food production. Designing MCSs for Vertical Farming with Solar Light (VFSL) delivers energy-saving benefits but is constrained by inter-layer shading, which limits productivity and conflicts with yield requirements. Therefore, optimal conceptual design is crucial. To address how to ensure complex designs meet stakeholder requirements during conceptual design, this study proposes a Digital Twin-driven Generative Design (DTGD) framework. The framework links stakeholder requirements with system architecture, fully incorporating theories related to system architecture, Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE), The Double Diamond (TDD), and Digital twin (DT). Using Digital Twin Modeling (DTM) and Candidate Architecture Decision (CAD) as core methods, it supports the generation and trade-off analysis of multiple Candidate Architectures (CAs). When applied to the design of MCSs in a case study, two CAs (square and zigzag cultivation) are generated. Within a design-stage DT model (an early-stage DT) for light simulation, key A-Frame design variables, including A-Frame Width (FW), A-Frame Height (FH), and the vertical height difference between adjacent planting containers (PCVH), are optimized to identify the optimal design solution. Cultivation experiments using the designed MCSs in a greenhouse in Handan, China, confirmed normal growth of cream lettuce in a single cycle. Based on this empirical data, the estimated annual production potential reaches 49.78 kg·m⁻²·year⁻¹ (assuming ten annual cropping cycles), satisfying the stakeholder yield requirement. This demonstrates the framework's practical feasibility for the evaluated case. Future work may incorporate Large Language Models to enhance automated design generation and explore alternative MCSs for wider urban adoption.

candidates.title: Mesh2Shell Neural Operator for Inverse Shape Optimization
candidates.abstract: Physics-driven design seeks high-performing geometries, which need not conform to a learned shape category. Parametric and latent-space approaches facilitate surrogate-based optimization, but restrict deformations to prescribed shape families or learned decoders. We introduce the Mesh-to-Shell Neural Operator (M2S-NO) as the mesh-to-shell component of a category-agnostic inverse shape optimization framework. We separate the explicit mesh used for design from the volumetric representation used for physics prediction. M2S-NO maps oriented surface samples to a surface-centered shell representation, such as TruncatedSDF or HeatSDF. A separate problem-specific PDE neural operator (PDE-NO) maps this representation to physical fields. Objective gradients update mesh vertices through both operators, without a latent shape decoder. Preconditioning and remeshing support free-form deformation, while fixed interfaces are controlled directly on the mesh. Optional shell-space proposals enable topology changes. We evaluate geometric matching, jet-engine brackets, and neutron moderators, with independent FEM and OpenMC evaluation. Relative to the best training designs, M2S-NO reduces maximum bracket displacement by 14.3% and increases neutron-sensor current by 13.8%. Optimization also succeeds from an out-of-distribution bracket initialization, demonstrating the framework's geometric flexibility.

candidates.title: Composable CAD: Sketch-to-CAD Program Synthesis in Parts
candidates.abstract: Designers often build CAD models part by part, and may iterate on individual components throughout the design process. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) can synthesize CAD programs from sketches, but generating parts independently does not ensure that they are composable: components may lose the intended proportions and alignments or fail to join correctly where they meet. We present Composable CAD, a framework that uses off-the-shelf VLMs to synthesize a design space of independently sampled, interchangeable component programs, where any selection composes into a coherent CAD model. We recover design constraints from the sketch and use them to construct a coarse proxy that establishes how the components are sized, aligned, and attached. We then generate each component independently from its proxy and apply a deterministic rewrite to ensure that neighboring components meet at their prescribed interfaces. We evaluate Composable CAD across a range of objects and sketch styles and conduct two user studies. Compared to VLM-only baselines, our method produces more detailed, composable designs.

candidates.title: Inverse design of architectural floorplans with gradient-based optimization of binary subdivision graphs
candidates.abstract: Computer-aided floorplan synthesis automates a core task in architecture and construction planning: balancing room programs, connectivity, areas, and boundary constraints. The fuzzy nature of machine-learning models makes it difficult for generative methods to achieve the precision and predictable edits needed in architectural design. Building on a hypergraph representation coupling binary subdivision graphs with access graphs, this paper proposes a gradient-based inverse-design workflow for controllable floorplan synthesis. Its differentiable soft-split formulation converts subdivision parameters into continuous room masks, allowing room areas and compactness to be optimized while preserving a prescribed or retrieved subdivision structure. Compared with non-differentiable optimization, this method is faster and performs favorably on several connectivity metrics. Residential floorplan experiments show improved access satisfaction and area accuracy over existing methods. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated across several design scenarios, supporting interactive computer-aided design and controllable layout synthesis for early-stage decision making under varied design requirements.

candidates.title: CAD-WAM: Anticipating Geometry for Text-to-CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from text requires selecting operations that produce the intended changes to the geometry constructed so far. An incorrect operation can compromise subsequent steps, making reliable multi-step generation challenging. Existing methods based on large language models (LLMs) primarily learn to predict commands, without explicit supervision of the geometric states those commands should produce. Inspired by world-action models, we introduce CAD-WAM, which couples geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction. We define complete modeling operations as actions in a CAD domain-specific language (DSL) and encode surface point clouds of intermediate solids into compact latent states using a pretrained variational autoencoder. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the target description and current geometric state, while an auxiliary head on the same backbone predicts the next state to provide geometric supervision during training. We construct step-wise training trajectories from parametric CAD models in the DeepCAD dataset, pairing each trajectory with an expert-level textual description. At inference, each generated action is executed by a CAD kernel, and the resulting solid is re-encoded to inform the next decision. On the DeepCAD test set, CAD-WAM outperforms the task-specific baselines in geometric accuracy and output validity, with larger gains on models requiring more operations, and produces more accurate geometry than general-purpose LLMs prompted with the same DSL. Ablations further show that next-state supervision reduces mean Chamfer distance by 13.2\% relative to an otherwise identical model trained only to predict actions. candidates.title: CAD-WAM: Anticipating Geometry for Text-to-CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generating editable computer-aided design (CAD) models from text requires selecting operations that produce the intended changes to the geometry constructed so far. An incorrect operation can compromise subsequent steps, making reliable multi-step generation challenging. Existing methods based on large language models (LLMs) primarily learn to predict commands, without explicit supervision of the geometric states those commands should produce. Inspired by world-action models, we introduce CAD-WAM, which couples geometry-conditioned action generation with next-state prediction. We define complete modeling operations as actions in a CAD domain-specific language (DSL) and encode surface point clouds of intermediate solids into compact latent states using a pretrained variational autoencoder. An LLM backbone generates the next action from the target description and current geometric state, while an auxiliary head on the same backbone predicts the next state to provide geometric supervision during training. We construct step-wise training trajectories from parametric CAD models in the DeepCAD dataset, pairing each trajectory with an expert-level textual description. At inference, each generated action is executed by a CAD kernel, and the resulting solid is re-encoded to inform the next decision. On the DeepCAD test set, CAD-WAM outperforms the task-specific baselines in geometric accuracy and output validity, with larger gains on models requiring more operations, and produces more accurate geometry than general-purpose LLMs prompted with the same DSL. Ablations further show that next-state supervision reduces mean Chamfer distance by 13.2\% relative to an otherwise identical model trained only to predict actions. candidates.title: Co-Construction of Production-Line AAS Geometric Models and Knowledge Graphs Driven by a Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Digital twin systems for a production line usually run on two models at once: an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) that holds asset information under IEC 63278, and a knowledge graph (KG) that records device topology and process semantics. On real projects, though, the two are built apart from each other. Engineers key the AAS geometric model in by hand from drawings and field measurements, while process engineers author the KG separately. The same data therefore gets entered twice, reuse is poor, and sooner or later the two models disagree. This paper presents a co-construction method that removes the duplication at its source. A fine-tuned vision-language model (VLM) reads the engineering sources a line already has, namely 2D/3D CAD drawings, on-site laser point clouds, and equipment technical manuals, and fills a standardized AAS; the KG is then derived from that AAS by fixed rules, so both models share one source. The method is arranged in four layers: multi-source data preprocessing with coarse-to-fine ICP spatial registration; LoRA-based domain adaptation of an open-source VLM supported by industrial prompt templates; automatic population of the AAS geometric, property, and connectivity submodels with conformance-checked .aasx generation on Eclipse BaSyx, plus QEM-based mesh simplification; and same-source KG derivation through fixed field-to-triple mapping rules, backed by a single-source constraint, automatic reconciliation, and incremental refresh with version traceability. We demonstrate the complete pipeline on a photovoltaic cell production line, and a parameterized Monte Carlo simulation of data consistency shows that, for manual single-entry error rates between 1% and 10%, conventional dual-entry modeling produces 4–39 times more data inconsistencies than the proposed single-source derivation, with the gap widening as the error rate grows. The method offers a reusable and extensible path toward production-line digital twin modeling; empirical validation on a physical line is planned as future work.

candidates.title: Automation of Tunnel Support Detailing with AI-Assisted Programming
candidates.abstract: Drafting tasks in geological engineering are time-consuming and often highly repetitive, with tunnel support drawings being a representative example. Although such tasks may appear straightforward and intuitive to experienced engineers, translating drafting logic into executable code typically requires substantial software development effort. While modern CAD and BIM platforms provide programming and automation capabilities, their effective use has traditionally depended on skilled programmers rather than domain engineers. This paper presents a practical case study in which a geological engineer with only basic programming experience leveraged recent advances in artificial intelligence, specifically large language models, to develop a custom code for automating tunnel support drawings. The workflow generates detailed support layouts directly from the tunnel contour and a limited set of user-defined engineering parameters, such as bolt spacing, liner thickness, and support class. Crucially, the approach preserves engineering judgement by requiring the engineer to define all design parameters and to review the final outputs, while automating repetitive drafting operations. The results demonstrate a viable pathway for lowering the barrier to engineering automation. The proposed approach is readily extendable to similar repetitive drawing tasks across a broad range of geological engineering applications.

candidates.title: Single-Image 3D Mesh Reconstruction via Point-Aware Diffusion (SPAR3D) and Bezier Spline Vectorization (SVG/EPS/DXF) for Engineering and Industrial Design Education
candidates.abstract: Abstract (ERIC 5-Element Standard): The purpose of this study is to evaluate browser-based single-image three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and raster-to-vector contour tracing for computer-aided design (CAD), rapid prototyping, and additive manufacturing instruction. The methodology examines Stable Point-Aware 3D (SPAR3D) architecture—which couples point-cloud diffusion sampling with triplane mesh reconstruction—across 50 object categories (DS-3), alongside cubic Bezier spline quantization into Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG), Encapsulated PostScript (EPS), and Drawing Exchange Format (DXF) for computer numerical control (CNC) laser cutting. Results demonstrate that SPAR3D reconstructs watertight textured 3D meshes averaging 42,500 to 61,500 vertices in a mean inference time of 6.20 seconds directly in a web browser, while vector tracing reduces geometric contour error below 0.42 pixels. By offloading neural point-cloud generation from local workstations to browser endpoints, vocational and engineering programs eliminate the requirement for 24-gigabyte VRAM GPUs. Implications for STEM and CTE curricula include accessible 2D-to-3D fabrication workflows. Additional materials include 6 tables, 34 references, CAD lab protocols, and 190 embedded URI links.
