candidates.title: CardioHolisticAI for multimodal deep learning based coronary artery disease risk stratification and personalized treatment recommendation
candidates.abstract: Despite the significant reduction in mortality and morbidity caused by coronary artery disease (CAD), early stratification of risk is important for timely intervention and individualised care. Most current CAD prediction methods rely on clinical variables, focus on single-modality analysis or simple fusion, and lack interpretability, calibration, and robustness assessment. The authors introduce CardioHolisticAI, a multimodal deep learning framework that also features MultiRiskNet for CAD risk stratification in Low, Medium, and High risk. MultiRiskNet leverages modality-specific encoders and attention-guided fusion to combine clinical features, modality-agnostic radiomic descriptors, and genomic pathway information while maintaining modality-specific representations. A multilevel explainability module integrates SHAP-based global importance, Integrated Gradients-based local attribution, radiomic feature ranking, and pathway-level genomic analysis. MultiRiskNet was evaluated with repeated five-fold cross-validation and achieved an accuracy of 98.50 ± 0.16%, a Macro-F1 score of 0.985 ± 0.0015, and a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 0.992 ± 0.0009, outperforming all evaluated unimodal and conventional fusion baselines. Noise injection, feature masking, and repeated-initialisation experiments suggest stable performance under the assessed internal conditions, and calibration analysis examined the reliability of the predicted probabilities. This is because the imaging source is non-cardiac and the source modalities are independent and not clinically validated at the patient level. Before clinical deployment, external evaluation in a patient-linked multimodal cardiac cohort is needed. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Impact of super resolution deep learning reconstruction with a 1024 matrix on CAD-RADS classification of intermediate coronary stenosis: A bicentric retrospective study
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Moderate coronary stenosis (CAD-RADS 3) is a diagnostic gray zone in coronary CT angiography (CCTA). We evaluated whether super-resolution deep learning reconstruction (SR-DLR), particularly with a 1024 matrix, modifies CAD-RADS classification and inter-reader agreement. Materials and methods: Thirty-nine CCTA examinations from two centers, each containing at least one 50-69% stenosis identified on the routine normal-resolution deep learning reconstruction (NR-DLR), were reconstructed with NR-DLR and SR-DLR (512 and 1024 matrices). Five experienced readers blindly assigned CAD-RADS categories. Agreement was assessed with Gwet's AC2 and paired reclassification with exact McNemar tests. Subgroup analyses (plaque composition, initial image quality) were exploratory. Results: Forty-six lesions were analyzed (19 calcified, 16 mixed, 10 non-calcified, one in-stent). Agreement remained excellent (AC2 0.89 [0.86-0.92], 0.87 [0.83-0.90] and 0.84 [0.81-0.88] for NR-DLR, SR-DLR-512 and SR-DLR-1024). Consensus CAD-RADS 2 rose from 6.5% to 21.7% with SR-DLR-1024 (p = 0.016; 10 lesions downgraded, 2 upgraded), predominantly in lesions with non-calcified components. Per-reader CAD-RADS 2 rates ranged from 13% to 30%, increasing significantly for two of five readers (p = 0.004). Conclusion: SR-DLR-1024 modified CAD-RADS classification in about one fifth of intermediate lesions while preserving excellent agreement. Without an invasive reference standard, these reclassifications reflect a change in reader interpretation rather than a proven gain in accuracy.

candidates.title: Explainable Multimodal AI Approach to Reduce Unnecessary Breast Biopsies
candidates.abstract: Recently, there has been rise in multimodal vision-language models for computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), yet their application in breast diagnosis, particularly for predicting biopsy outcomes remains limited. This study presents a multimodal vision-language approach, incorporating Grad-CAM as an Explainable AI (XAI) technique, to predict benign tumors in patients recommended for biopsy, especially those classified as BI-RADS 4 and 5. A novel multimodal framework was devel- oped using Vision Transformer (ViT) for imaging feature extraction and DeBERTa-V3-Large for textual embeddings. The model was trained and evaluated on a comprehensive in-house dataset comprising 1,632 patients, each with four mammography views and a corresponding radiology report. The features of both modalities were extracted independently and fused by late fusion before classification. Grad-CAM was used to generate visual explanations highlighting key regions influencing model predictions. The proposed model demonstrated high sensitivity 90%, 95%, 99%, and 100% with corresponding specificities of 40%, 36%, 18%, and 11%, respectively. The best AUC achieved was 0.72 by multimodal approach on the test set, outperforming the image only (0.66) and text-only (0.68) baselines. The proposed multimodal architecture, enhanced with Grad-CAM, demonstrates a strong potential to identify benign tumors among high-risk patients, offering interpretable insights and thereby helping reduce unnecessary biopsies, patient anxiety, and healthcare costs.

candidates.title: Copying As Defense: Protecting Images from Editing By Eliciting Model Copying
candidates.abstract: Image editors built on diffusion transformers (DiTs), such as Flux Kontext, make it possible to turn a single photograph into a convincing manipulated image, including harmful and non-consensual edits. Proactive defenses aim to prevent such manipulations by adding an imperceptible perturbation before an image is shared. Existing defenses for DiT-based in-context editors make the output attend less to the protected reference image. But this leaves the model free to follow the edit instruction using the text and its own generated tokens, often producing a new, weakly grounded image rather than preventing the edit. We find that the opposite strategy is more effective: instead of leading the model to ignore the reference, we encourage it to copy it. Through controlled attention interventions, we show that concentrating target-token attention on the reference image in only a few early blocks is sufficient to collapse the editing behavior, causing the model to reproduce its input, often as a lossy copy, rather than execute the requested transformation. Based on this insight, we introduce Copying-as-Defense (CaD), which maximizes per-token target-to-reference attention mass in early transformer blocks. Since attention rows are normalized, increasing reference attention suppresses the attention allocated to the text and generated canvas. Restricting the objective to early blocks also lets us truncate the backpropagation path, keeping optimization cheap. Across editors and benchmarks, CaD reduces average edit success from 81.4% on unprotected images to 24.0%, a 70.6% relative reduction, and by a further 44.3% relative to DeContext, the strongest baseline (43.0%). CaD is also roughly 1.8-2.0x faster per optimization step than comparable methods.

candidates.title: Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling: A Material-Removal-Centric Framework for Three-Dimensional Shape Generation
candidates.abstract: Three-dimensional shape generation has been studied through a variety of representations and learning paradigms, including voxel-based generation, point-cloud synthesis, implicit neural representations, neural radiance fields, Gaussian-based scene representations, and procedural computer-aided design (CAD) generation. Despite their differences, many approaches primarily formulate generation as the direct synthesis or reconstruction of a target representation. This paper proposes Subtractive Trajectory Generative Modeling (STGM), a material-removal-centric framework that formulates three-dimensional shape generation as the progressive transformation of an initial stock into a target solid through a sequence of removal operations. Instead of generating the final geometry exclusively as a static representation, STGM models the evolving residual material state, the geometry of each removal region, the ordering of operations, and the compatibility of each operation with manufacturing constraints. The framework combines a geometric state representation, a conditional removal policy, differentiable or approximately differentiable geometric updates, and a multi-objective optimization procedure. Its objectives include target-shape fidelity, preservation of required material, operation complexity, accessibility, and estimated manufacturing cost. A hierarchical strategy is proposed to organize coarse removal, intermediate structural formation, and fine geometric refinement. The paper defines a formal problem, presents a reference algorithm, specifies a training objective, and develops an experimental protocol for evaluating geometric accuracy, trajectory quality, manufacturability, and computational efficiency. STGM is presented as a research hypothesis rather than an empirically validated method. Its potential contribution lies in integrating material-state evolution and removal-sequence optimization into a unified generative formulation, while its novelty and effectiveness require systematic comparison with existing CAD sequence generation, constructive solid geometry, machining-aware modeling, and shape-generation approaches.

candidates.title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Rapid differentiation of ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke subtypes is vital for acute management. Although current deep learning models achieve high single-dataset accuracy, they suffer from "shortcut learning" and domain shift in external validation. This study proposes a hierarchical computer-aided diagnostic (CAD) system mimicking emergency triage. Methods: We introduce a 3-channel Radiology-Focused Preprocessing pipeline that feeds radiological Hounsfield Unit (HU) windows into Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) backbones via asymmetric formats (.mat and .png). The architecture utilizes a novel joint cross-attention fusion network optimized by an Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss. Results: Our system achieved a 95.48% F1-score on the internal stroke dataset. However, multi-center external validation (AISD, BHSD, PhysioNet) using a Mask Anchor filter revealed a drop to the 58-62% range, exposing the "internal validation illusion" caused by hardware noise. Critically, models exhibited high precision (77%) but low sensitivity (57%) for ischemic stroke, proving prone to hemorrhage overdiagnosis. Multi-seed variance analysis demonstrated that the DenseNet201+ViT backbone yielded the lowest deviation (0.59) and highest stability, making it the most reliable architecture for real-world clinical integration. Conclusions: To overcome diagnostic challenges, future research must focus on multimodal architectures that combine 3D volumetric extraction with clinical data.

candidates.title: Fidelity metric with 3D shape descriptor for digital twin standardization
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive framework for assessing Digital Twin (DTw) fidelity through multi-modal deep learning, evaluating the correspondence between physical manufactured components and their digital CAD specifications. Six diverse vision architectures CLIP-ViT-B/32, ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16, MobileNet-V2, ResNet-50, and EfficientNet-B0 were systematically evaluated using complementary metrics: cosine similarity for visual pattern matching, Descriptor Distance Index (DDI) for embedding space discriminability, and 3D geometry scoring via symmetric chamfer distance. The methodology integrates three data modalities: high-resolution multi-view photography, structured light scanning point clouds, and CAD model specifications. CLIP-ViT-B/32 demonstrated superior overall performance with the highest fused verification score (0.7868), excelling in cross-modal visual understanding between physical images and CAD renders. ViT-B/32 and MobileNet-V2 exhibited exceptional embedding space robustness with remarkably low DDI scores (0.0056 and 0.0037 respectively), while maintaining competitive cosine similarity. All models except ResNet-50 achieved optimal performance at 96-pixel input resolution, indicating efficient feature extraction at moderate scales. The integrated verification framework, combining visual, geometric, and embedding metrics through weighted fusion (F = 0.4C + 0.3(1-D) + 0.3G), provides a comprehensive assessment methodology for digital twin validation. These findings demonstrate that model selection should be guided by application priorities: CLIP-ViT-B/32 for visual-semantic understanding, ViT architectures for embedding space robustness, and MobileNet-V2 for computationally constrained environments. The proposed multi-metric approach advances standardization of fidelity assessment in precision manufacturing and digital twin implementation.

candidates.title: EDA-Agent: A Multi-Agent AI System for RTL Verification, Circuit Debugging, and Semiconductor Design Automation -TCAD-2026-2322 (IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems)
candidates.abstract: Hardware verification and debugging traditionally consume over 70% of digital Integrated Circuit (IC) design cycles. Engineers spend thousands of hours manually parsing static timing reports, inspecting Value Change Dump (VCD) waveform traces, and writing SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA). EDA-Agent is an open-source, multi-agent AI platform designed to automate Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code analysis, functional testbench generation, waveform failure debugging, synthesis area estimation, and timing slack optimization. To overcome the hallucination risks of pure neural generation, EDA-Agent employs a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture that combines Large Language Models (LLMs) with strict deterministic boundaries: AST Static Analysis: A custom regex/AST parser deterministically evaluates design violations, such as latch inference conditions and blocking assignment race hazards. Trace-Based VCD Waveform Debugging: The system parses standard IEEE 1364 VCD files to build a temporal transition matrix, allowing the agent to back-track state transitions and map assertion failures directly to faulty source code lines. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG): The system grounds its reasoning in an indexed database of IEEE 1800-2017 SystemVerilog standards, Yosys manuals, and OpenSTA documentation. Empirical evaluations of EDA-Agent demonstrate 100% unit test accuracy on core parsing components, 94.2% waveform-based bug localization accuracy, and a 37.5x acceleration in SystemVerilog testbench generation compared to manual human workflows.

candidates.title: Dual-graph computable knowledge engineering for CAD-to-CNC macro synthesis
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can synthesize G-code, but autonomous CAD-to-CNC macro-generation must preserve geometry, process constraints, variable roles, equations, loop bounds, coordinate mappings, and controller syntax. This paper presents a dual-graph computable knowledge engineering method in which typed knowledge objects are selected by a semantic relation graph and converted by a computational dependency graph into acyclic variable-expression-loop dependencies. A seven-layer Macro-Structured Parametric CNC Code (Macro-SPCC) schema and Macro-Program Intermediate Representation (MPIR) organize the evidence, while deterministic modules perform evaluation, geometric checking, and FANUC Macro B compilation. Across 12 tire-mold lettering-insert tasks from six DXF cases and two toolpath configurations, the method achieved 91.7% accuracy, 50.0 percentage points above Text-RAG, and a 100.0% compilation pass rate. VERICUT confirmed continuity, endpoint reachability, and safe retraction, demonstrating a traceable, computationally closed, and executable synthesis process.

candidates.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
candidates.abstract: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD, a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that renders node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.

candidates.title: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design of Electronic Devices and Circuits
candidates.abstract: Abstract Driven by the miniaturization of single components, which has reached few nanometers, chips can nowadays accommodate hundreds of billions of transistors. As a result, modern nanoelectronics devices and systems are becoming extremely complex. To remain truly effective, computer-aided design (CAD) tools must evolve in parallel with these advancements, keeping pace with the increasing demands of scale and functionality. In recent years, machine learning (ML) has seen an incredible development in several areas. In nanoelectronics, ML is already offering promising technological solutions that improve performance and provide predictions across the entire electronic design stack. From material properties to quantum transport and circuit behavior, ML techniques are making simulation workflows much more efficient and flexible, leading to a new paradigm of CAD: Machine Learning Computer-Aided Design. This review examines the latest developments in computer simulations for assessing the performance of electronic systems and the types of models used across the different levels of abstraction. We also discuss the challenges that still need to be addressed, especially the need for physics-based ML models, and explore future directions toward generative machine learning frameworks tailored specifically for electronic system design.

candidates.title: Joules-to-GDP: How Much Economic Value Do AI Systems Produce per Unit of Energy?
candidates.abstract: AI systems are increasingly used to complete economically valuable tasks in various professions, such as software engineering and finance. This motivates the question: how much economic value does an AI system produce per unit of energy? To answer it, we introduce Joules-to-GDP, a framework that measures output dollar value minus AI execution cost per unit of energy, which we call Net Value per Joule (NVJ), and expert time saved per unit of energy, or Time Saving per Joule (TSJ). We then apply the framework to 220 GDPval tasks across 44 occupations. Four findings stand out. First, the most valuable work is not always the most efficient. For example, engineering work such as CAD design yields about 10% more net value per task than software development such as building websites, yet the latter yields about 27% more per joule. Second, defaulting to the most capable model can mean less total value from the same energy budget. Of the five tested models, GLM 5.2 delivers the most net value, $72.27 per task on average, using the energy of about four hours of active laptop use, while Gemma 4 31B achieves 56% of that with 23% of the energy, for 2.5x the NVJ and 2.8x the TSJ. Third, for the same model, NVJ and TSJ vary widely across different accelerators, and adding GPUs can raise energy use for modest gains: eight H100s use 3.2x the energy of one to cut completion time by only 22%, at similar net value. More capable models and more hardware must therefore earn their extra energy with enough gains in output value. Finally, the work of experts who use AI is harder for AI to match than that of experts working alone. Measured against it, GLM 5.2's NVJ falls by 70% and its TSJ by 65%. Taken together, these findings justify economic return per joule as an objective for selecting professional tasks and improving language models and accelerators, and as a basis for examining AI's effect on the economy

candidates.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
candidates.abstract: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.

candidates.title: Mitigating Query Shortcuts in Chain-of-Thought with Context-Aware Decoding
candidates.abstract: While Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), recent studies have shown that final answers do not always depend on the generated rationales. In particular, LLMs may rely on query-specific shortcuts rather than the information provided by their reasoning steps. In this paper, we investigate whether context-aware decoding (CAD), an existing contrastive decoding method, can mitigate such shortcut behavior when applied to CoT reasoning. We study this application as Rationale Contrastive Decoding (RCD), which contrasts the next-token distributions conditioned on the query with and without its rationale, amplifying tokens whose likelihood increases due to the rationale. We provide a theoretical interpretation of this decoding rule via a KL-regularized reward-maximization objective. Experiments across five reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that RCD improves answer accuracy over standard CoT. Furthermore, intervention analyses using ground-truth and random rationales reveal that RCD increases the behavioral dependence of final answers on the rationale content. Our findings suggest that contrastive decoding offers a simple, training-free approach to mitigating query shortcuts.

candidates.abstract: Generative Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently exhibit non-deterministic variances when generating spatial geometries, rendering them susceptible to structural hallucination in production CAD pipelines. This paper introduces Synthetic Environment Infrastructure (SEI)—a deterministic compiler architecture converting natural language parametric constraints into validated blueprints via Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs), Domus Mare FEA hydro-envelopes (180 kN·m capacity), and Think Furniture joinery compilation.

È un pannello del trittico Leonardo’s Spatial Grammar, insieme a Leonardo’s Rulers e a Leonardo’s Score: tre indagini nate separate, una sola grammatica metrico-modulare dello spazio. Quella utilizzata da Leonardo da Vinci per costruire i suoi spazi prospettici. Il corpus, depositato su Zenodo, contesta l’idea di una prospettiva albertiana a scacchiera applicata in modo uniforme. Metodo La ricerca adotta un approccio di retroingegneria: parte da ciò che è visibile e misurabile nelle opere per ricostruire i principi metrici e modulari che ne organizzano lo spazio. Funzione dell’app L’app è uno strumento di supporto alla ricerca accademica: non la sostituisce, ma la integra, rendendone più accessibili e immediatamente comprensibili i risultati più significativi. From the Annunciation through the Adoration to the Last Supper, Leonardo leaves in the picture the modules he measured with: ashlars and tiles (inserted geometry), the 4:3 mesh (revealed geometry), the rhythms of the tapestries and coffers (tuned geometry). candidates.title: Generative AI for Mechanical Systems Design: A Systematic Review of Language-Driven, Diffusion-Based, and Physics-Informed Approaches — Protocol for a Two-Tier Systematic Map and In-Depth Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Protocol of a systematic review on generative artificial intelligence for the design of mechanical systems, components and structures (2021–2026). The review covers three paradigms: language-driven approaches (large language models, vision-language models, LLM agents, CAD-as-language models), diffusion-based approaches (denoising diffusion, latent diffusion, flow matching) and physics-informed generative approaches. It uses a two-tier design: (1) a systematic map of all eligible studies, coded by paradigm, design task, design stage, design representation and evaluation type; (2) an in-depth critical synthesis of a core set of studies that quantitatively evaluate the physical validity, constraint satisfaction or manufacturability of generated designs, selected with criteria fixed before full-text assessment. Reporting follows PRISMA 2020. Searches were run in Scopus and Web of Science on 20 October 2026; this registration was made after title/abstract screening and before full-text assessment and data extraction.

candidates.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
candidates.abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

candidates.title: COMPUTER AND ENGINEERING GRAPHICS IN TRANSITION THROUGH A BIBLIOMETRIC AND THEMATIC REVIEW OF DISTANCE EDUCATION RESEARCH
candidates.abstract: Distance learning is increasingly relevant in technical education, particularly in engineering and computer graphics. The integration of digital technologies enables the development of students’ spatial visualization and creative design skills essential for modern engineering practice. This review examines how distance education has transformed teaching and learning in these fields by analyzing global studies from 2014 to 2025. Although online delivery presents challenges in visualization and interactivity, advances such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation-based environments, and virtual laboratories are helping to bridge these gaps. The review identifies diverse program types, ranging from foundational design graphics to advanced applications in artificial intelligence, data science, and augmented reality. Despite significant progress, limited empirical evidence exists on learning outcomes and engagement. Through bibliometric analysis, this study maps thematic trends and collaboration patterns, offering evidence-based insights to enhance the quality and accessibility of engineering graphics education in the digital era

candidates.title: OV-PEAR: Observation-Verified Pose-Scale Estimation and Reconstruction for Unknown Industrial Manipulation Objects
candidates.abstract: Fine industrial robotic manipulation requires 6D pose, scale, and an operation-ready 3D model. Existing industrial pose estimation relies on CAD models, object-specific training data, or stable workcells, limiting use with unseen objects; zero-shot methods suffer from single-view occlusion, generative bias, and scale uncertainty. We present OV-PEAR, an observation-verified framework for 3D reconstruction and pose-scale estimation of unknown industrial objects. Its three-stage object-centric pipeline: (1) segments RGB-D instances and generates object-level 3D hypotheses; (2) anchors them to the robot frame via appearance-aware view retrieval, explicit scale search, and visibility-sensitive registration; (3) back-projects multi-view RGB-D evidence into the object-canonical frame to verify voxel occupancy, suppress hallucinations, and produce reusable trusted object models. On BOP-Industrial, OV-PEAR achieves 0.657 average AR and improves pose and voxel-level geometric consistency in real scenes; real-robot connector assembly reaches 99.67% grasp and 84.00% assembly success. The model library and pose-scale log enable short-term object-level state maintenance at 0.02 ms/frame.

candidates.title: Assessing the CAD Capabilities of General-Purpose AI Models: A Case Study of GPT-6 Astra
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI models and agentic systems have enabled them to perform some CAD tasks. A systematic assessment is now needed to establish what these systems can accomplish and how well their outputs meet engineering requirements. This paper presents an empirical study of GPT-6 Astra, a SOTA general-purpose AI model, across four basic CAD tasks: model understanding, generation, editing, and evaluation. We design test cases spanning different levels of complexity and engineering requirements. The results show that GPT-6 Astra can support multiple stages of CAD workflows, with successful outcomes in cases involving nontrivial geometric complexity. This suggests that general-purpose AI is beginning to offer practical value in almost all steps in CAD workflow. However, gaps remain between generating visually plausible geometry and producing valid, functional, and editable CAD models. Recurring errors in freeform geometry, parameter dependencies, and mating relationships between parts limit engineering usefulness. Agentic iterative refinement can improve results but does not consistently resolve critical errors; long completion times further constrain practical use.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering-Grade Parametric CAD: A Critical Review of Representations, Large Language Models, and Agentic Design Systems
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly expanding computer-aided design (CAD) from shape generation toward generative, conversational, and agentic engineering. However, most AI–CAD evaluations remain dominated by geometric similarity and execution success, while industrial CAD depends on editable parameters, design intent, stable feature histories, manufacturing constraints, and downstream CAD/CAE reuse. This structured critical review synthesizes 107 sources, principally from 2020–2026, across constrained sketches, boundary representations (B-Reps), parametric sequences, executable CAD programs, large language and multimodal models, CAD agents, commercial-CAD integration, and CAD–CAE. Rather than organizing the field only by model family, the review compares methods through the engineering information preserved and the behavior of generated models after modification. The synthesis identifies a consistent evidence gap: geometric validity and program execution are increasingly strong, whereas native feature-tree robustness, persistent references, design-intent preservation, and downstream verification remain weakly benchmarked. To address this gap, we propose the engineering-grade AI–CAD (EG–CAD) framework, in which geometric validity and executability are mandatory gates followed by parametric editability, constraint/design-intent preservation, feature-history robustness, engineering compliance, and downstream usability. A reference agent architecture and staged roadmap connect these criteria to CAD/CAM/CAE and smart-manufacturing workflows, reframing AI–CAD as an engineering automation problem rather than a shape-generation task.

candidates.title: CRAFT: Corrective and Robust Multi-Agent Framework for Text-to-Parametric CAD
candidates.abstract: Text-to-CAD generation has the potential to make mechanical CAD more accessible, but existing approaches face a trade-off between data dependence and output fidelity. Supervised methods rely on large paired text-model datasets, while zero-shot prompting strategies are often brittle and tend to lose the parametric structure needed for downstream editing and customization. We present CRAFT, a corrective and robust multi-agent framework that produces parametric OpenSCAD programs from natural language without task-specific training. At its core is a JSON intermediate representation that carries symbolic parametric expressions throughout the generation process, so the resulting models remain editable and retain their parametric structure. CRAFT combines semantic understanding, parametric planning, compilation, rendering, self-correction, and component-level verification within a layered recovery process, using multi-view visual feedback to detect and repair geometric errors. Across NopSCADlib, ABC, and Slice-100K, CRAFT is competitive with direct zero-shot baselines in perceptual and geometric quality while exposing substantially more editable parametric structure.

candidates.title: Foundation models in reverse engineering, CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing: A systematic review
candidates.abstract: Reverse engineering is undergoing a profound transformation driven by the emergence of foundation models. These models, together with their applications, are progressively extending the limits of artificial intelligence (AI) from geometrical reconstruction to a more sophisticated level engineering reasoning. In contrast to traditional methods, which usually use sequences of algorithms for specific 3D retrieval and reconstruction tasks, current foundation models train geometrical representations that are able to support semantic reasoning, computer-aided design (CAD) reconstruction, and intelligent manufacturing in a unified way. This work provides an overview of foundation models within the context of reverse engineering and their combination with CAD reconstruction and additive manufacturing. Starting from a systematic bibliometric analysis of the recent literature, the present review is mainly focused on the development of representation learning and reviews the key geometric forms that are being used by the current foundation models. The paper also explores the engineering abilities facilitated by such models in the reverse engineering process. Furthermore, current challenges, research obstacles, and future directions are critically explored, emphasizing the recent transition toward intelligent engineering systems. The analysis shows that foundation models are gradually making reverse engineering move from being an assortment of discrete computational activities to becoming an engineering process workflow that is made possible by means of geometry representations and multimodal reasoning as well as engineering AI. Finally, considerations on the importance of developing engineering conceptual frameworks to interpret the emerging role of foundation models in future intelligent engineering systems are drafted.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence applications in photon-counting detector CT for coronary artery disease imaging: a narrative review
candidates.abstract: Background and Objective: Coronary artery disease (CAD) remains the leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is a first-line non-invasive imaging modality for CAD evaluation, but conventional energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) is often limited by blooming artifacts, noise, and partial-volume effects. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) provides superior spatial resolution, reduced blooming, and multi-energy spectral data, yet its ultra-high-resolution (UHR) datasets frequently suffer from increased noise and complex spectral information that require advanced processing. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising solution to fully exploit PCD-CT's advantages. This narrative review aims to synthesize the current evidence on AI applications in PCD-CT for CAD imaging, evaluate their technical performance and clinical potential, identify limitations, and propose future directions. Methods: A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase, supplemented by hand-searching of reference lists. Original English-language studies applying AI techniques to PCD-CT data for CAD imaging were included, and categorized using a 5-level translational framework. Key Content and Findings: Thirty single-center studies were identified and grouped into three main categories. In image quality improvement, denoising models achieved 60-96% noise reduction while preserving spatial and spectral fidelity. Radiomics studies (the largest group) identified specific texture features in myocardium, plaques, pericoronary, and epicardial adipose tissue associated with coronary artery calcium severity, hypercholesterolemia, aging, and CAD presence, although feature reproducibility was only moderate. Automated detection/quantification/segmentation tools demonstrated high reproducibility, improved stenosis quantification, substantial workflow benefits, and promising CT-fractional flow reserve (FFR) performance with strong intra-individual agreement to EID-CT. Conclusions: AI has shown promising technical advancements when applied to PCD-CT for CAD imaging. However, the evidence base remains limited by small sample sizes, single-center and single-scanner designs, lack of external validation, and absence of outcome-driven studies. Future research should focus on multicenter prospective validation, standardized protocols, human-in-the-loop systems, and clinical impact assessment to support the safe and effective translation of AI-enhanced PCD-CT into routine clinical practice.

candidates.title: An algorithm for 6D object pose estimation based on generative single-image 3D reconstruction
candidates.abstract: Reliable 6D object pose estimation is a foundational capability for robotic manipulation in Industry 4.0 and unstructured warehouse environments. Current state-of-the-art methods, such as PVN3D and SAM-6D, predominantly rely on “Model-Based” paradigms that necessitate high-fidelity CAD models of the target objects for training or template matching. This requirement severely limits their applicability in open-world scenarios where such CAD models are unavailable in real-time. To bridge this gap, a novel 6D Pose Estimation Framework without fine-tuning on the target object (Zero-Shot) is proposed to eliminate the dependency on prior CAD models. A single-view 3D generative model is leveraged to synthesize a geometrically plausible 3D mesh from a single RGB image. To address the scale ambiguity inherent in generative models, which poses a critical challenge for robotic grasping, a Template-Prior Iterative Closest Point (TP-ICP) based on the classical ICP is introduced for iterative recovery of the metric scale. This algorithm robustly recovers the metric physical scale of the neural-generated mesh using depth information, employing median-based outlier removal and template-guided ICP to handle occlusions and sensor noise. The recovered metric mesh is then seamlessly integrated into a standard 6D pose estimation pipeline, establishing a closed-loop framework comprising model self-generation, metric scale calibration, and pose estimation. A fully reproducible implementation scheme is presented. Systematic experiments on the LINEMOD dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves robust 6D pose estimation suitable for robotic tasks, even in the complete absence of prior CAD models.

candidates.title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
candidates.abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

candidates.title: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling
candidates.abstract: Mechanical Design & CAD Explained: Engineering Design & Digital Modeling is an open-access, accreditation-aligned curriculum module developed under the PREP4UNI.ONLINE OER Initiative for undergraduate engineering candidates, mechanical designers, and STEM educators. Structured in accordance with the Washington Accord, EUR-ACE, and IEA Global Engineering Competency frameworks, this module bridges fundamental mechanics of materials with modern 3D CAD modeling, finite element simulation, and design for manufacturing. Key Analytical & Technical Coverage: Continuum Failure Theories: Von Mises distortion energy multi-axial yield criteria, Modified Goodman and ASME elliptic dynamic fatigue limits, and preloaded bolted joint compliance. Machine Element Synthesis: Circular power transmission shafting under combined torsion and bending, Marin endurance limit factors, stress concentration factors, and 1D worst-case vs. RSS statistical tolerance stack-up analysis. Digital Design Paradigms: Parametric feature modeling, generative topology optimization, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for real-time stress feedback, and Model-Based Definition (MBD) standards (ASME Y14.5 / STEP AP242). Applied Pedagogy: 4-column systems engineering trade-off matrix, seven cross-sector industrial failure case studies across aerospace, automotive, energy, and robotics, an interactive HTML5 canvas beam stress simulator, and six multi-step quantitative worked examples with explicit engineering interpretations. candidates.title: INTEGRATION OF GENERATIVE DESIGN AND PARAMETRIC MODELING IN CAD FOR OPTIMIZATION OF AEROSPACE COMPONENT STRUCTURES
candidates.abstract: This paper discusses modern approaches to the design of load-bearing structures for aerospace equipment using topology optimization and generative design methods. The need to integrate parametric modeling to ensure the manufacturability of complex geometric shapes is sub-stantiated. It is shown that the application of additive technologies in combination with generative design allows reducing the weight of components by 40–50% while maintaining their strength characteristics.

candidates.title: Beyond overall accuracy: subgroup performance and threshold calibration of AI-assisted chest radiography for equity-oriented pulmonary tuberculosis screening
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted computer-aided detection (CAD) can expand access to chest radiography interpretation for pulmonary tuberculosis screening and triage, but high overall discrimination does not ensure safety at a deployed threshold. This focused narrative Mini Review synthesizes evidence on subgroup performance, threshold calibration, external validity, and implementation of CAD for adult pulmonary tuberculosis. Smear-negative, asymptomatic, and some HIV-associated disease may be less radiographically visible, increasing false-negative risk. Conversely, previous tuberculosis and competing chronic abnormalities reduce specificity and concentrate unnecessary confirmatory testing. Sex, age, geography, clinical setting, verification design, and software version can further alter operating performance. A numerical threshold is therefore not a portable algorithm property but a context-specific clinical resource-allocation policy. We propose a lifecycle in which programs define the intended use, lock the product and version, conduct representative local validation, select an operating point under explicit sensitivity and capacity constraints, audit clinically relevant subgroups, and monitor the complete care pathway. Stratified thresholds and multivariable models may improve selected settings, but current evidence does not justify replacing robust local calibration and governance. Prospective evaluations should compare threshold strategies under common verification standards and report missed cases, referral burden, treatment initiation, and patient-important outcomes.
